goal: Fix the application so every test in tests/test_acceptance.py passes. Do not edit that file; read the QA handover notes for the failing behaviour.

decisions.why: All 87 tests in tests/test_acceptance.py pass on the current tree, and the other 407 tests pass when run separately
decisions.evidence: python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_acceptance.py (87 passed, 409.94s); python3 -m pytest -q --ignore=tests/test_acceptance.py (407 passed, 470.25s); sha256sum of tests/test_acceptance.py matches a250fc6c…

tried_and_failed.what: Started the full suite with a trailing & inside a background Bash call
tried_and_failed.why_it_failed: The shell exited and the pytest process did not survive; the log stayed empty. I used run_in_background on the pytest command itself instead.

assumptions: Ticket 500's only recorded problem was a missing handover JSON, not a test failure
Running the acceptance file and the rest separately is equivalent to the single-session check.py qa run
open_questions: If the orchestrator's check.py qa still fails, the cause is probably load or ordering flakiness (the hover tests test_AC_52 and test_AC_59 were flaky in earlier tickets) that only shows in one combined session. Please share its output_tail.

lessons.lesson: When a fix ticket's QA handover has no failing tests listed, run the acceptance file and the rest of the suite before changing code. The cause may be a missing handover JSON, not a bug.
lessons.when: A ticket says to fix failing acceptance tests but gives no failure output
lessons.evidence: handovers/ticket-500-run-591.json problems: 'agent did not end with the handover JSON'; both test runs green

lessons.lesson: Start long test runs with run_in_background on the pytest command itself, then wait with an until-grep DONE loop. A backgrounded & inside a foreground command is killed when the shell exits.
